newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ariane to launch INTELSAT satellite on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Ariane to launch INTELSAT satellite on Wednesday.

text.p: Western Europe's 96th Ariane rocket is scheduled to blast off from French Guiana on Wednesday carrying a satellite for the 140 member-nation INTELSAT organisation, the Arianespace company said on Monday.
The INTELSAT 802 satellite weighs 3.4 tonnes and will provide telephone and television services to the Indian ocean region. It was built in the U.S. by Lockheed Martin Telecommunications.

The launch is set for between 8.45 p.m. and 9.41 p.m. (2345 Wednesday and 0041 Thursday GMT) from the European Space Agency launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America.
The Paris-based Arianespace company said it has 43 heavy satellites on order to be launched worth an estimated $3.4 billion.
